args: Restage only; no release. Identify the SAME cream-cheese carton printed face and the two physical Cream/C short-end corners c0/c1 using supplied identities, NOT stationary projections. Return end_pixels in physical c0,c1 order and end_camera. Request p0..p5 as six spread-out actual depth samples wholly on that face, away from seams/fingers; these are plane samples, not correspondences. Identify b0, the bowl interior large pale floor medallion center, and b1, the separate bottle-side rear inner-wall rosette. Request their depth only if unambiguous. Initially use bowl_mode rim: request d0..d3 as spread-out valid upper-lip surface depths and select eight well-distributed INNER opening boundary rim_pixels in rim_camera. Do not sample the sloping interior as the lip plane. After motion, same upright bowl plus current known marks can validate the existing opening; if marks are obscured, substitute a fresh rim measurement instead of repeating obscured marks. Assess the visible closed-assembly route: initial vertical rise of 20 to 60 mm followed by fixed-attitude translation over the bowl; at the raised approach assess one additional tilt of at most 0.32 rad. opening_corridor asks whether fingers and outward jaw corridors of 20 mm per side are visibly free above the rim and away from the bottle/other bodies, including a short upward withdrawal corridor, not whether release has succeeded. Do not infer hidden clearance or hidden carton corners. Unknown is allowed. Current observation purpose: fresh pre-translation validation

end_identity_reference.scope: Physical identity reference only; after movement these pixels are not current measurements.

reference.uncertainty_scope: The 0.4 mm measurement floor is a conservative operational floor, not calibrated confidence. Historical carton dimensions bound unseen extent; current short-edge width, plane residual, feature spread and identities revalidate their use.

result.explanation: The current wrist image shows the Cream printed face and its visible C-end short edge. c0 is the left physical corner and c1 the right physical corner, consistent with the supplied identities; these are current boundary selections, not projected historical positions. The bowl is upright and its two specified marks are distinguishable. No external obstruction is visible in the local upward-rise and raised fixed-attitude translation route toward the bowl. Robot self-occlusion limits the finger-corridor assessment. This is pre-translation validation only, not approval of release or of a later tilt.

parameters.notes: p0..p5 are six current printed-face plane samples, not correspondences. c0/c1 identify the visible Cream/C short end; the opposite end is self-occluded and is not inferred. Check corner depth patches for boundary mixing. b0 is the large pale floor medallion center; b1 is the separate bottle-side rear inner-wall rosette. Fresh d0..d3 and eight inner-boundary pixels are supplied for the initial rim model. Use only upper-lip surface depths in the narrow d patches, excluding background and sloping interior. Bowl identity and upright appearance agree with the supplied reference; metric stationarity remains a depth check. Closed-route clear describes the visible local raised route, not hidden geometry or a full-scene certificate. The 20 mm outward jaw corridors and short withdrawal cannot be fully seen because of robot self-occlusion, so opening_corridor is unknown, not an observed obstruction. Assess any additional tilt of at most 0.32 rad at the raised approach using its then-current evidence. Regions contain silhouettes and require object segmentation; bowl_visible_surfaces is not a lip-plane sample region. Closure alone does not establish retention. No release is authorized.
